questions.q: What exactly does the fix change about rule FW-0231?
options: It deletes the rule entirely
It changes the destination port from 3389 to a different port
It narrows the configured source from 198.51.0.0/16 to the vendor's real 198.51.100.16/28, with no other change
It adds a brand new rule alongside the old one
questions.explain: The fix is a scope correction only -- the rule's purpose and port stay the same.

questions.q: Why does a one-line scope edit still go through a change ticket?
options: It doesn't need one since the edit is small
Because this exact rule caused the incident, so it deserves a second set of eyes and a recorded justification before going live
Change tickets are only required for new rules, never edits
Owen requires a ticket for unrelated budget reasons
questions.explain: The rule's history of causing the incident is exactly why its edit gets the same formal review discipline Lesson 12 makes standard going forward.

questions.q: What does Test 1 (the vendor's real connection) confirm?
options: That the old broad range is now blocked
That the legitimate vendor connection still succeeds -- the fix didn't break production
That the correlation rule from Lesson 5 still fires
Nothing -- Test 1 is not part of validation
questions.explain: Test 1 proves the fix didn't break the legitimate business need the rule exists for.

questions.q: What result from Test 2 (the old-range address) actually proves the fix closed the gap?
options: DeviceAction == Allow, same as before
No log entry at all
DeviceAction == Deny, showing the address is no longer inside the rule's range
A new alert firing in Sentinel
questions.explain: A Deny result for an address outside the new, narrower range is the proof the exposure is actually closed.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say a fix tested only one way is half-validated?
options: Because testing is always unnecessary
Because confirming the vendor still connects proves you didn't break production, but only confirming the old broad range is now denied proves you actually closed the gap
Because only the negative test matters at all
Because the positive test alone is sufficient proof of a correct fix
questions.explain: Either test alone could let a bad fix look successful -- both are required to validate the change.
